# Calcaneal fracture

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Surgery > Trauma and orthopedic surgery > Lower extremity > Calcaneal fracture*

[Original Article Link](/library/fF0kh3)

---

## Summary

<u>Fractures</u> of the <u>calcaneus</u> are caused by acute trauma or chronic load-bearing on the foot. <u>Fractures</u> may be extraarticular (e.g., avulsion of the <u>calcaneal</u> process) but more commonly involve an intraarticular surface (e.g., the subtalar <u>joint</u>). Acute <u>calcaneal</u> <u>fractures</u> are typically caused by a high-energy impact to the heel (e.g., fall from a significant height, <u>motor vehicle accident</u>); a low-energy impact may cause a <u>fracture</u> in an <u>osteoporotic</u> or diseased bone. Clinical manifestations of an acute <u>fracture</u> include heel <u>pain</u> and <u>plantar</u> <u>ecchymosis</u>. <u>X-rays</u> typically confirm the diagnosis, but a CT should be obtained if clinical suspicion for an acute <u>fracture</u> is high and the initial <u>x-ray</u> findings are negative. Orthopedics should be consulted early, and the affected extremity should be elevated and placed in a bulky dressing. Surgical treatment may be required for displaced or intraarticular <u>fractures</u>.




For details about <u>stress fractures</u> in the <u>calcaneus</u>, see “<u>Calcaneal stress fractures</u>.”
